'''Jean-Yves Jaffray''' (1939–2009) was a French [[mathematician]] and [[economist]] who made influential contributions in the fields of [[decision theory]] and [[mathematical statistics]].<ref name=Bouyssou>A. Bouyssou et al., Decision Making Process: Concepts and Methods</ref><ref name=Cohen>M. Cohen, Tribute to Jean-Yves Jaffray</ref> He pioneered methods in decision theory such as [[linear utility theory for belief functions]],<ref name=Jaffray>Jaffray, Jean-Yves (1989). "Linear utility theory for belief functions"</ref><ref name=Giang>P.H. Giang, On Jaffray’s Decision Model for Belief Functions</ref> bridging the gap between expected utility and the [[maximin rule]] by using [[subjective probability]] to encompass [[belief function]]s.<ref name=Bouyssou/>
